data.narrative:
World Labs, founded by Fei-Fei Li and team, is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company that has raised $1.23B+. The valuation analysis draws from a comparative set of 9 private and 1 public company (Palantir, PLTR), with key private peers including Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI—all operating in the same AI & Software sector at Series A or Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $1.2B total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $4.4B, with a range spanning $2.0B (Field AI) to $25.0B (Reflection AI). The peer cohort exhibits substantial dispersion, reflecting early-stage valuation volatility in frontier AI.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $5.1B (high), with a median of $3.4B. Key uncertainties include the wide spread within the peer set—particularly Reflection AI's $25.0B outlier—and whether World Labs' specific technical differentiation and team composition warrant positioning closer to the peer median or the stage-progression floor. Further diligence on revenue trajectory and product-market signals would refine this range.
